The served stack (LLM RAG system, model client and the standard-library
adapter) was measured against a fake LLM server on the local machine that
enforces a rate limit and answers a rate-limit response with a retry hint
(Fig.~\ref{fig:runner}); these are not measurements of a real provider. One
worker took {{bench.sequential.wall_time_s|.3f}}\,s for the {{bench.n_cases}} cases and eight workers
{{bench.concurrent.wall_time_s|.3f}}\,s, {{bench.concurrent.speedup|.1f}} times faster. With the client's budget set to twice the
server's limit, the limiter absorbed {{bench.over_eager.server.rate_limited}} rate-limit responses and no case
failed, and a warm response cache answered the suite in {{bench.warm_cache.wall_time_s|.3f}}\,s without
sending a request.
